title: Close release-browser semantic and WebGL failure coverage

scope.subject: Release-level browser acceptance for navigation, journeys, responsive behavior and WebGL/runtime failure conditions

research_summary: Reuse the existing Playwright runner, runtime guard, sharding and reports. Add missing product-semantic cases for Hero/return, native landmark and black-hole travel completion, guided Journey controls, mobile navigation and reduced motion. Extend the current runtime hook with browser-native WebGL context-loss events and test it using the standard WEBGL_lose_context extension. Use Playwright route abort for deterministic critical-resource negative coverage. No new runner, reporter or browser framework is needed.

sources.finding: Playwright natively supports viewport/device and reduced-motion emulation, including per-test media emulation.
Playwright route.abort provides deterministic resource-failure injection without a proxy or custom network harness.
page.evaluate executes browser-side code and can invoke WebGL APIs directly in the page context.
The standard webglcontextlost event reports loss of a WebGL drawing buffer.
The standard WEBGL_lose_context extension can deterministically simulate context loss for tests.

search_ladder.conclusion: No external browser-quality platform adds needed value because the repository already has sharded Playwright, traces, screenshots, runtime hooks and cloud reports.
Playwright already covers functional scenarios, viewport/reduced-motion emulation, request failure injection, page-side evaluation and per-test diagnostics.
Existing Playwright sharding and GitHub runners remain the execution subsystem; missing value is semantic coverage, not another CI topology.
Browser-native WebGL context loss events plus WEBGL_lose_context provide the correct failure signal and deterministic injection mechanism.

candidates.name: Existing Playwright release scenarios
candidates.reason: Adds semantic release cases to the existing runner and preserves current traces/screenshots/reporting.

candidates.name: Playwright route/emulation/evaluate primitives
candidates.reason: Covers resource abort, responsive/reduced-motion behavior and browser-side failure injection without new infrastructure.

candidates.name: WebGL native context-loss APIs
candidates.reason: Provides the actual runtime failure event plus a standards-based deterministic simulation extension.

coverage_matrix.capability: Journey, return, landmark and native travel semantics
coverage_matrix.decision: Add independent Playwright release tests against real product state and DOM/dataset contracts.
Use Playwright's native viewport and reduced-motion emulation inside dedicated release cases.

coverage_matrix.capability: Critical resource and WebGL failure detection
coverage_matrix.decision: Use route.abort plus runtime WebGL event capture; negative tests pass only when the expected fatal signal is observed.

decision.rationale: Close product release coverage with the existing Playwright stack and standards-based browser hooks. This adds no CI framework and keeps each failure independently diagnosable.
decision.fallback: If a product-semantic case exposes a real application bug, keep the test and create a separate approved product fix rather than weakening the assertion.
